verdicts.why: A plain geographical noun; naming a body of water says nothing about the speaker's attitude toward it.
A technical pigment term with no attitude beyond its meaning; the sentences show the water sense, but the printed sense is neutral either way.
A technical name for a specific red pigment; it describes a substance and does not judge it.

In the printed adverb sense ('just plain wrong') it is an informal intensifier meaning unmistakably; the judgement lives in the adjective it modifies, and its informality is register, not attitude toward the thing.
A mathematical term for a number; wholly descriptive.
The name of a currency unit; no attitude is carried by naming it.
The name of a historical coin; descriptive only.
Names the act of remaining in expectation; being kept waiting may be unpleasant, but the word itself takes no side (a bad referent, not a loaded word).
